combined_ratio.definition: Loss ratio plus expense ratio; the primary measure of underwriting profitability
combined_ratio.formula: Combined Ratio = Loss Ratio + Expense Ratio
combined_ratio.interpretation: Below 100% = underwriting profit; above 100% = underwriting loss

loss_ratio.definition: Incurred losses divided by earned premiums

persistency_rate.definition: Percentage of policies remaining in force year-over-year

lapse_rate.definition: Percentage of policies terminated by policyholder; inverse of persistency

placement_rate.definition: Applications issued divided by applications submitted times 100%

ibnr.definition: Incurred But Not Reported reserves; actuarial estimate of claims that have occurred but not yet been reported

rbc_ratio.definition: Risk-Based Capital ratio; regulatory minimum capital requirement per NAIC

underwriting_cycle_time.definition: Days from application to underwriting decision

orsa.name: Own Risk and Solvency Assessment
orsa.purpose: Enterprise risk assessment; supplements formulaic RBC with forward-looking analysis

rag_chunks: Combined ratio equals loss ratio plus expense ratio. Below 100% indicates underwriting profit; above 100% is an underwriting loss. Healthy target is <100%, world-class is <95%. Loss ratio is incurred losses divided by earned premiums (healthy 60-75% for P&C). Expense ratio is underwriting expenses divided by written premiums.

Persistency rate measures policies remaining in force year-over-year (healthy 85-90%). Lapse rate is policies terminated by policyholder (inverse of persistency). Placement rate is applications issued divided by submitted (healthy 70-80%). These are key life insurance operational metrics.

IBNR (Incurred But Not Reported) reserves are actuarial estimates of claims that have occurred but not yet been reported. Estimation methods include chain ladder, Bornhuetter-Ferguson, and frequency-severity. Reserve adequacy compares actual reserves to required reserves per Risk-Based Capital (RBC) regulations.

RBC ratio should be >150% (regulatory minimum plus buffer). ORSA (Own Risk and Solvency Assessment) is a NAIC requirement for forward-looking enterprise risk assessment, supplementing the formulaic RBC calculation. Together they form a two-pillar solvency framework. Related frameworks: ERM, COSO.

NAIC Annuity Suitability Model requires best interest standard. Variable annuities need SEC registration and prospectus. FINRA oversees broker-dealer sales practices. Suitability factors: age, risk tolerance, liquidity needs, financial situation. State-specific surrender charge limits apply.

Chief Actuary role: Quantitative Risk Expert. Reserve estimation uses chain_ladder, Bornhuetter_Ferguson, frequency_severity methods. Confidence levels: best_estimate, reasonably_likely, adverse. KPIs: reserve_adequacy within actuarial range, pricing_accuracy (A/E ratios). Vocabulary: Loss Triangle, IBNR, RBNS, Development Factor.

Chief Risk Officer role: Enterprise Risk Guardian. Risk acceptance authority: within_appetite=autonomous, at_boundary=consult_CEO, exceeds_appetite=board_approval. Considerations: probability, severity, correlation, concentration. Frameworks: ORSA, ERM, COSO. KPI: RBC ratio > regulatory minimum + buffer.

Claims handoff chain: FNOL → Adjuster (assignment 4h, contact 24h). If fraud indicators → SIU (24h acknowledgment). If reserve exceeds threshold → Reinsurance (30-60 day treaty timeframe). Large loss → L3 management escalation. Reserve development → Chief Actuary notification.
